title: It worked in staging

alert.title: web: 18% of page loads failing
alert.summary: Since the 2:10 PM release, about one in five page loads shows an error.

clues.title: Deploy history
lines: 14:10 web v2.18.0 released to every server at once

clues.title: Errors by country
lines: Only visitors who see prices in pounds or euros hit the error.

actions.label: Restart the web servers
actions.feedback: Every server comes back on v2.18.0 and the errors continue.

actions.label: Add more web servers
actions.feedback: More servers run the same broken code. Still 18% of page loads fail.

actions.label: Write a quick fix and ship it straight to production
actions.feedback: The untested fix breaks dollar prices too, and errors jump to 60% before you notice.

actions.label: Turn off euro and pound prices
actions.feedback: Errors stop, but UK and EU customers now see prices in dollars and support calls pile up.

actions.label: Roll back to v2.17.4
actions.feedback: Errors fall to 0.1% within two minutes.

rootCause.summary: Version 2.18.0 broke prices shown in euros and pounds, and staging only tested dollars, so the bug reached every production server at once.
keyPoints: the 2:10 PM release caused the errors
only euro and pound prices failed
staging did not test other currencies
the release went to every server at once

lesson: When errors start right after a release, roll back first and debug later. A staging setup that matches production, and releasing to a few servers first, catch this before customers do.
